papers.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
papers.abstract: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.
papers.llm_summary: Đánh giá cost-aware abstention cho phân loại ticket IT: chính sách TF-IDF + ngưỡng chọn trên calibration data giảm 38% expected cost và wrong-route từ 15.3% xuống 3.5%, beat LLM prompting trên corpus 47.837 ticket.
papers.llm_reason: Experiment quy mô lớn với model cost thật (0/1/9) và CI rõ ràng, kết quả nghiêng hoàn toàn về business: classifier rẻ + ngưỡng beat LLM — actionable thẳng cho mọi quyết định automation ROI và chọn model theo expected cost chứ không accuracy.

papers.title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. Multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown growing potential in this domain by leveraging collaboration and verification among multiple LLM agents. However, existing evaluations primarily focus on the correctness of final answers in text-only settings, offering limited insight into multimodal reasoning capabilities, the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, and robustness against reasoning errors. To address these limitations, we introduce MAMath-Bench, a process-aware benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities of MASs. MAMath-Bench comprises 1,003 problems spanning 11 mathematical categories, multiple difficulty levels, and several modalities, including text, images, and audio. It features fine-grained milestone annotations to evaluate systems across three dimensions: problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final-answer accuracy over strong single LLMs. Second, collaboration can substantially enhance the coverage of intermediate reasoning, but such gains may come at the cost of increased reasoning redundancy. Third, current systems remain vulnerable to adversarial reasoning errors, particularly those involving subtle structural perturbations. The dataset is available at https://github.com/mira-ai-lab/AgentMath.
papers.llm_summary: Xây benchmark MAMath-Bench với 1.003 bài toán đa phương thức để đánh giá multi-agent math reasoning theo độ đúng đáp án, độ tin cậy quá trình reasoning và robustness trước nhiễu adversarial.
papers.llm_reason: Benchmark thật, quy mô lớn, metric fine-grained; phát hiện 'multi-agent không luôn thắng single LLM mạnh' là insight cực kỳ actionable cho người chọn kiến trúc làm sản phẩm/content, dù gắn với giáo dục toán.

papers.title: Asking a Multimodal LLM Whether Someone Fell: Zero-Shot Screening of Low-Resolution Thermal Video in a Laboratory and an Occupied Home
papers.abstract: Thermal cameras can watch over older people living alone without capturing faces, and multimodal large language models (LLMs) can judge a short video without task-specific training. We evaluate a production multimodal LLM, Gemini 3.8 Flash at temperature 0, as the decision stage of an event-triggered fall screener, used exactly as a deployed prototype uses it: one request per short thermal clip, with its sound track when there is one, and its predecessor Gemini 3.7 Flash on the same requests. On 438 staged falls and 563 non-fall windows that we located by hand in a public 32x24 thermal dataset, the deployed request called 69% of the held-out subjects' falls (67% over all subjects; bed falls excluded) and none of 499 non-fall windows, including people lying on the floor and getting up. Over 76 h of ordinary life in an occupied room, recorded at 160x120 with sound, it called none of 395 clips a fall (95% upper bound 1.2 false alarms per day) and caught 4 of the 9 staged falls the camera could see. One cautionary sentence in the prompt ("a person who goes out of view ... is not a fall") accounted for many of the misses: removing it raised sensitivity on the held-out subjects from 69% to 83% on 3.8 Flash and from 80% to 92% on Gemini 3.7 Flash, and in the home from 4 to 9 of the 9 visible falls, with no false call in ordinary living but at the price of calling deliberate lie-downs a fall. Sensitivity collapsed at 8x6 pixels (34%); identical requests disagreed on 4% of windows; and when the model called a fall, its explanation placed it within a second of the annotated landing 99% of the time. Two conventional detectors trained on the laboratory data caught nearly every held-out laboratory fall but raised 14.2 and 23.9 false alarms per day in the home. We release the frame-level fall annotations of the public dataset and every model answer on it.
papers.llm_summary: Dùng Gemini 3.8/3.7 Flash zero-shot làm bộ sàng lọc té ngã từ video nhiệt độ thấp, test 438 té ngã + 563 cửa sổ thường và 76h sống thực, phát hiện một câu prompt cản trở nhiều lần miss.
papers.llm_reason: Multimodal LLM production zero-shot đúng core (30/35), benchmark thật lab+nhà với bound false-alarm và sensitivity theo subjects (24/25), care-tech là vertical content cho audience 30+ nên có góc khai thác nhưng không phải chess/content chính (10/20), cực kỳ actionable: thay một câu prompt nâng sensitivity 69→83% với chi phí false positive rõ ràng — bài học prompt engineering ngay lập tức dùng được (17/20).

papers.title: ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly deployed for complex, long-horizon tasks or emerge as a natural consequence of agents interacting in the wild. Yet they give rise to significant safety and security risks: the flexible protocols that enable task generalization also expose novel threats, from cascading prompt injection to inter-agent collusion. Progress in defending against these threats has been slowed by a lack of shared empirical infrastructure, which forces bespoke environment development for every new defense and makes standardized comparison impossible. Existing evaluations address isolated threat models or single-agent settings, but none jointly vary attack, defense, and architecture across realistic multi-agent environments. To address this gap, we introduce ORBIT, a configurable evaluation framework for empirical multi-agent safety and security research, built on UK AISI's Inspect. ORBIT lets researchers configure communication topologies, memory, scheduling, and agent roles. It supports four threat types and four defense strategies, as well as non-adversarial failures, with a benchmark suite spanning five scenario families covering browser use, computer use, agentic coding, customer service, and cooperative allocation. Our central finding is a gap in defense transferability across threats: per-action defenses that cut a compromised agent's attack success by 60 points on multi-issue coding give no measurable protection against colluding agents, and none of the defenses we tested generalized over all attacks tested. We further demonstrate security-performance tradeoffs and interactions between architecture and defense effectiveness. We make ORBIT available open-source at https://github.com/wlanderson0/orbit.
papers.llm_summary: ORBIT là framework đánh giá an toàn/bảo mật cho hệ thống multi-agent LLM, cho phép cấu hình topology, memory, vai trò agent và benchmark 5 họ tình huống thực tế (browser, coding, CS...).
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent security cực liên quan cốt lõi, có benchmark thật trên Inspect, insight 'defense ít transfer qua các loại attack' vừa làm content vừa dùng khi triển khai agent cho khách hàng.

papers.title: HiRS-Agent: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent System for Reliable Long-Horizon Remote Sensing Task Solving
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models and multimodal models have pushed remote sensing (RS) processing from simple perception models to agentic systems designed to tackle complex, long-horizon RS tasks. However, existing systems often rely on monolithic decision-making frameworks, which fail to accommodate the multi-stage, interdependent nature of RS tasks. This centralized approach leads to challenges such as unstable task execution, incorrect tool usage, and error propagation across stages. To address these issues, we propose HiRS-Agent, a hierarchical multi-agent system for long-horizon RS task solving. HiRS-Agent adopts a two-level collaborative architecture: the Manager Layer handles dynamic routing, step-level verification, replanning, and termination control, while the Specialist Layer organizes domain-specific tools according to the RS workflow and is responsible for subtask reasoning and tool execution. To further enhance the system's capability, we introduce a two-stage supervised tuning strategy and a verification-guided hierarchical reinforcement learning stage to jointly optimize coordination and tool-use policies. Experiments on Earth-Agent Benchmark and ThinkGeo show that HiRS-Agent substantially improves long-horizon tool-use capability and final-task correctness, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured multi-agent collaboration for reliable RS agents. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/IntelliSensing/HiRS-Agent.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất HiRS-Agent, hệ thống multi-agent phân cấp (Manager routing/verify/replan + Specialist tool execution) cho tác vụ remote sensing dài hạn, tối ưu bằng SFT và verification-guided RL.
papers.llm_reason: Đúng chủ đề hierarchical multi-agent + tool-use với experiment benchmark thật (Earth-Agent, ThinkGeo); pattern manager/specialist và replanning sau verify áp dụng được cho tự động hóa pipeline content agency.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Disentangling Decomposition from Typed-State Quality Assurance in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM pipelines are often credited with gains in software engineering tasks, but it is rarely clear whether a gain stems from the typed contract between agents or from the specialized prompts that decomposition enables. We study this attribution problem in Requirements Engineering, comparing three architectures for classifying requirements as functional or non-functional and then prioritizing them with MoSCoW: a single-call baseline; a two-call variant that reuses the pipeline's specialized prompts but passes an unvalidated intermediate; and a pipeline with a Pydantic-validated typed state. The 18 conditions cover PROMISE NFR+ (625 requirements), three locally hosted small language models, and two languages. The F1 gain over the baseline is associated with the two-call, specialized-prompt variant (up to +0.075), whereas the typed state adds a small difference (-0.003 to +0.013) that is significant in one of six comparisons. Beyond accuracy, the typed pipeline contains out-of-range model outputs at the agent boundary, while the unvalidated variant fails later and drops the requirement, and it shows a small, reproducible increase in inter-model MoSCoW consistency whose cause our design cannot isolate. The study is associative: the contrasts bundle prompts, call count, and staged context, and the results come from three 7--8B models on one dataset. The implementation and replication package are archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23380444).
papers.llm_summary: Nghiên cứu tách biệt xem lợi ích của pipeline multi-agent LLM đến từ việc phân rã nhiệm vụ (decomposition) hay từ typed-state validation, cho thấy specialized prompt qua hai lần gọi mới là yếu tố chính tạo ra gains.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan cốt lõi multi-agent, có experiment rõ ràng trên 18 điều kiện, insight 'đầu tư prompt specialization trước khi xây dựng typed state' rất actionable cho người làm content và xây workflow AI.

papers.title: Evaluating Scaffolding-Oriented Multi-Agent Large Language Model System for Clinical Interview Training
papers.abstract: Clinical education must prepare medical students to conduct safe and coherent patient interviews under conditions of uncertainty. Traditional standardized patient (SP) training is resource-intensive and difficult to scale. We developed a scaffolding-oriented multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) AI Standardized Patient (AI-SP) training platform1. The system includes a patient agent for simulated dialog, a tutor agent providing Socratic prompts without disclosing diagnostic information, and a turn-level evaluator agent that monitors clinical progress without revealing summative scores. In a randomized controlled study (N = 100 medical students), participants were assigned to either a multi-agent (MA) scaffolding condition or a control condition. All students completed two learning sessions under their assigned condition followed by an examination conducted in a patient only environment. Performance was assessed using a standardized Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) based rubric. While no significant difference was observed in final diagnostic accuracy between groups, the multi-agent AI standardized patient system improved final examination scores compared to the control group utilizing structured progressive information disclosure; the most substantial and consistent improvements were observed in communication, the expression of empathy, and specific history-taking behaviors. These findings suggest that specialized LLM agents enhance the process quality of simulated clinical interviews without artificially inflating examination outcomes. To support future research, we release a multi-expert annotated dataset comprising transcripts, checklist annotations, turn-level evaluations, and OSCE-aligned scoring outcomes. This resource aims to facilitate the development of pedagogically grounded AI-SP systems and advance research on AI-supported clinical reasoning training.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng nền tảng bệnh nhân chuẩn AI đa tác tử (patient-tutor-evaluator) để dạy phỏng vấn lâm sàng, thử nghiệm RCT 100 sinh viên và cải thiện rõ rệt giao tiếp, đồng cảm.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent LLM có experiment RCT chuẩn (OSCE) và cho insight thiết kế scaffolding/tutor agent transferable sang content training, nhưng domain y khoa xa business cá nhân.

papers.title: Self-Adapting Group of Experts for Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems bring together language model agents with different roles to propose, review, and refine solutions. Each agent's response depends on its model's capabilities, the reasoning strategy defined by its system prompt, and the information in its input context. Existing frameworks often adapt communication by changing this context while leaving individual prompts fixed, even when a problem calls for different skills. We study whether agents' initial responses can identify a strategy better suited to the current problem and guide its transfer to other agents. To address this, we introduce SAGE (Self-Adapting Group of Experts), a training-free framework that uses answer agreement, prefix consistency, and reciprocal peer review to select a strategy donor. SAGE transfers the selected donor's reasoning strategy to the other agents while preserving their original roles. This transfer uses only the agents' original system prompts, without access to the problem or generated solutions. After strategy adaptation, agents exchange responses through a dynamic, sparse directed acyclic graph that routes information from higher-scoring agents to lower-scoring agents. Experiments across multiple agent backbones and reasoning benchmarks show that SAGE achieves higher average accuracy than the evaluated baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/atifquamar07/sage.
papers.llm_summary: SAGE training-free chọn donor agent sự transfer reasoning strategy dựa answer agreement/prefix consistency/peer review rồi truyền qua DAG định hướng động, beat baselines trên nhiều backbone và benchmark.
papers.llm_reason: Self-adapting multi-agent reasoning đúng core (32/35), multiple agent backbones + reasoning benchmarks, có code GitHub (20/20), liên quan business khi bạn orchestrate agent content pipeline (9/20), rất actionable: training-free, transferable strategy, có code để thử ngay cho multi-agent setup (15/20).

papers.title: Decision4Rec: A Jev-Inspired Framework of Decision Models on Knowledge and Active Graphs for Multi-Agent Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Decision models, such as the commercial Jev, are language models that return one probability for each option of a question instead of generating text. We present Decision4Rec, an open and modular framework that makes decision models useful for recommendation. A knowledge graph writes the logs of each recommendation scenario as short statements on a defined scale, such as "sold: top 10%". A pool of agents, proposes candidates, and a residual ranker keeps the best 30. A decision model, trained once on real choices of three scenarios, reads them through one interface of typed questions, and a fusion step combines its answers with the score of the ranker. Any model with this interface can be used, and we run the commercial Jev, the released open Kev and Kev models trained by us on recommendation requests. The framework with a trained 4B decision model is 25 to 36% above the best trained baseline in NDCG@10 in three sparse Amazon catalogues, one of them never used to train the decision model, and almost tie with baselines on the dense Steam dataset. Most of the gain comes from the pool, and with a trained recommender it comes from what the agents know about its candidates rather than from new candidates. The 27B decision model adds to the pool 5 to 6% above the 0.8B model in three of four domains. A trained 0.8B open model beats the released Jev in eleven of fifteen settings and is never worse. On MovieLens-1M, a dense domain never seen in training, the gain is 5 to 7%. Code, configurations and trained models are available at https://github.com/marcopoli/decision4rec and https://huggingface.co/m-polignano.
papers.llm_summary: Decision4Rec dùng decision models (return probability per option) kết hợp pool agent + ranker cho recommender system, model 4B đạt cao hơn baseline 25-36% NDCG@10.
papers.llm_reason: Agent + recommendation rất khớp business multi-channel/content; experiment thật trên Amazon/Steam, insight 'pool of agents biết về候选' và 'small trained model beats commercial' actionable cho cá nhân làm content curation.

papers.title: Cloud and On-Premises Deployment of Uzbek Legal RAG via Targeted Retriever Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Deploying large language models for legal question answering raises challenges that general-purpose leaderboards do not capture, particularly for low-resource languages and under hard operational constraints. We report on building and operating a retrieval-augmented (RAG) legal assistant for Uzbek that must run in two regimes: a managed cloud service that maximizes answer quality within a per-token cost ceiling, and an on-premises deployment for clients whose legal data may not leave their infrastructure, restricting us to open-weight models on limited local hardware under latency constraints. Because no evaluation existed for this setting, we build two domain benchmarks: a retrieval benchmark of 178 expert-annotated legal queries with gold provision spans, and an end-to-end benchmark of 504 expert-curated question--answer pairs scored by an LLM judge whose ratings we validate against human judgments and against an independent-family judge. Applying these benchmarks under each regime, we find the open-versus-proprietary gap is small and cheaply closed by fine-tuning. Therefore, we train UTE-1, which is a state-of-the-art text embedder among open models for Uzbek. We also demonstrate that closing the performance gap via fine-tuning is both impractical due to the intensive hardware demands of long-context legal Q\&A and unnecessary, given that legal acts change frequently. We support this by reporting a negative result from a QLoRA experiment. We distill practical guidance for similar deployments, drawn from a system serving real users in production. We release our benchmarks, evaluation code and the fine-tuned embedder (UTE-1) \href{https://metric-ai-lab.github.io/Uzbek-Legal-RAG/}{at this https URL} to support future work on low-resource legal NLP.
papers.llm_summary: Triển khai RAG legal tiếng Uzbek ở cả cloud (giới hạn cost/token) lẫn on-prem (hardware hạn chế), xây benchmark retrieval 178 query + E2E 504 QA, train embedder UTE-1, kết luận gap open-vs-proprietary nhỏ và đóng bằng fine-tuning rẻ.
papers.llm_reason: R cực kỳ thực tiễn cho solopreneur: benchmark tự xây, LLM-judge validated, trade-off cloud/on-prem, cost ceiling, và bài học 'fine-tune nhỏ thay vì model lớn' rất actionable cho content AI.
